newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls on Americans to respect verdict.
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls on Americans to respect verdict.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday night urged Americans to respect the verdict in the civil trial of O.J. Simpson as he underscored a need for racial unity.
The verdict was announced at a Santa Monica, California, courtroom just as Clinton was finishing an hour-long State of the Union speech with an appeal for racial harmony.
The jury blamed Simpson for the brutal killings of his ex-wife and her friend and ordered him to pay $8.5 million in compensatory damages.

Told of the verdict after he spoke, Clinton told White House spokesman Mike McCurry that his reaction was the same as it was when Simpson was found innocent of any criminal wrongdoing 16 months ago in the slayings of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman.

"He said, 'My reaction is almost identical to the previous reaction, that we have to respect the jury verdicts that Americans bring in a situation like this, and it's time to move on and address the larger issues that confront America and that's what I attempted to do in my State of the Union address tonight'," McCurry said Clinton told him.
In his speech, Clinton said that building "one America" is the country's most important mission.
"Money cannot buy it. Power cannot compel it. Technology cannot create it. It can only come from the human spirit," he said.
